# Target uniqueness for branching tests

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`branching-target-uniqueness` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](branching-target-uniqueness.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Where branching tests tell apart the configurations of a target frame, a configuration of any source frame passes the same branching tests as at most one target configuration; likewise for likeness.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A branching test is nothing, a claim, the failure of a test, two tests together, or that some step by a move leads to where a test holds; configurations of two frames pass the same branching tests where every such test holds at the one exactly where it holds at the other. (`Becoming.BranchingTest`, `Becoming.BranchingTest.Holds`, `Becoming.SameBranchingTests`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
2. For any two frames, with no finiteness of their steps assumed: where branching tests tell apart the configurations of the target (any two passing the same branching tests are equal), a configuration of the source passes the same branching tests as at most one target configuration. (`Becoming.SameBranchingTests.functional`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
3. For any two frames: where likeness tells apart the configurations of the target (any two alike configurations of it are equal), a configuration of the source is alike to at most one target configuration. (`Becoming.Alike.functional`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Any two frames of the spine with the same moves and claims; the target frame is separated by branching tests, or for the likeness law by likeness.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Configurations passing the same branching tests need not be alike: where a move has infinitely many outcomes, two configurations can pass the same tests and not be alike. Witness: `Becoming.Unbounded.not_alike`.
- Uniqueness of the matching configuration does not make the target frame the one right description of the source.
- The law is for these branching tests; a richer test language must keep its own semantics, as the tests with parts do.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used.

<a id="next--下一步"></a>
## Next

Give, for an application, the target frame its branching tests separate, so that each observed configuration has one matching target configuration.
